name: Pan-Fried Soup Dumplings (Sheng Jian Bao)
desc: Fluffy yeasted buns filled with pork and dashi soup jelly, steamed and pan-fried in one skillet until the bottoms are crisp.

source.title: Pan-Fried Soup Dumplings (Sheng Jian Bao)
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 1 tsp vegetable oil, for the bowl and hands
250g soup jelly (all of the above), cubed
2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus a drizzle
3 tbsp Chinese black vinegar, for dipping

steps: Soup jelly: simmer the ginger, water and dashi powder in a small covered saucepan for 5 minutes. Meanwhile soak the gelatin leaves in cold water for 3 minutes.

Take the pan off the heat, squeeze the gelatin dry and stir it in until dissolved. Pour into a shallow bowl and remove the ginger. Once cool, freeze 20 minutes, then refrigerate 1 hour, until very firm.
Dough: mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the warm water and stir with a wooden spoon until a dough forms.
Work it quickly on the counter for 2 minutes with a slap technique: slap the dough down, stretch it into a long rope, fold it back into a ball, and repeat without tearing the rope.
Oil a bowl and your hands, shape the dough into a ball and set it in the bowl. Cover with a damp towel, wrap in a second towel, and let rise somewhere warm for 45-60 minutes.

Filling: put the pork, ginger, garlic, spring onions, both soy sauces, oyster sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, white pepper, salt and water in a bowl. Stir in one direction with a fork until it comes together in one mass. Chill.
Cut the soup jelly into pea-size cubes and fold them into the filling. Refrigerate until needed.

Mix the dusting flour and cornstarch. Punch down the dough, roll it into a log, and cut into 13 pieces (about 30g each). Roll into balls on the dusted counter, cover with a damp towel, and rest 5 minutes.
Dust again and roll each ball into a round about 10 cm (4 inches) across, the size of your palm. Keep them covered.
Coat the base of a 10-inch lidded nonstick skillet with 2 tbsp oil.
Put a heaped tbsp of filling on a wrapper and pleat the edges tightly together at the top so there are no gaps. Set it seam side down in the pan. Repeat, filling the pan in a circle.
Cover the buns with a damp towel and let them rise in a warm place for 15 minutes.

Pour room-temperature water into the pan until only the tops of the buns poke out. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then lower to medium and cook 10 minutes, until most of the water has evaporated and the filling reaches 160°F.
Sprinkle with the spring onions and sesame seeds, drizzle a little oil around the edge, cover and cook 30 seconds more. Check that the bottoms are deep golden and crisp.
Set the hot pan on a cold, wet towel for a minute to help release the buns, loosen them with a spatula, and flip onto a plate crisp side up. Serve with black vinegar and chili oil.
tips: The slap-and-stretch knead is what makes the buns fluffy.
Pinch the pleats tight: any gap lets the soup leak out and burn in the pan.
No black vinegar? Mix rice vinegar and soy sauce 3:1.
Freeze any leftover filling for the next batch.
